title: Rayburn Wright, Eastman and college life
summary: Wright left New York for Eastman; Sauter considers a college setting.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: There must be an out. Part of this has come about because of technology and we're not used to it; technology and music is quite a recent thing.

I guess that's one reason, as we talked before, Rayburn Wright left New York and went up to the Eastman because he wanted to--rather than working with blase in New York he said he'd rather work with less experienced and more enthusiastic people.
What I gather from the people I've talked to there is that there is nothing in Rochester besides Eastman.

There must be something he likes about being there. I wouldn't like to live in Manhattan--I've never done it--but I wouldn't like to have to either. If I could be in a college environment without being an educator that I probably could take too, and might even enjoy it.
That depends on what you mean by being an educator.

Well, it's what you're forced to be pretty much. If I had to pretend to be someone or something I'm not equipped really to teach, I prefer not to do it and I wouldn't like to have to do it to make a living.
